CallUsage.description:
Per-call consumption.

`call_seconds` is measured caller-join → caller-leave, not from the session
row's lifetime: `ended_at` is stamped after recording stops, a settle delay
and an artifact upload, all of which would otherwise bill as talk time.

The model names are recorded because they are configurable at runtime, so
the rate that applies is a property of the call, not of today's config.
CallUsage.title: CallUsage

Direction.description:
Which side placed the call.

BROWSER is not a third side — it is the console's mic with no PSTN leg at
all. It exists because a test call recorded as `inbound` is indistinguishable
from a voter's, which silently mixes rehearsals into the campaign's numbers.
Direction.title: Direction

TranscriptTurn.description: One parsed turn, numbered from 1 so an analysis can cite it.
TranscriptTurn.title: TranscriptTurn

VoiceArtifactReport.description:
What the bytes behind a session actually are.

Distinct from `VoiceSessionDetail.recording_available`, which only reports
that a URI was written. The post-call pipeline needs the difference: the
agent writes both URIs even on the failed path, so a call that dropped
before any audio and a call with a full recording look identical on the row.
VoiceArtifactReport.title: VoiceArtifactReport

VoiceTranscript.description: The call's turns, parsed once by the reader that owns the format.
VoiceTranscript.title: VoiceTranscript

get.description:
Report what a call's stored artifacts actually contain.

Read-only and tenant-scoped exactly like playback. The post-call pipeline
calls this instead of trusting `recording_uri`, so `recording_state=ready`
on a ticket means these bytes were opened, parsed and found to be a call.
Serve a call's parsed turns to the authenticated caller.
